title: feedback-bootleg-sprint-latch-2026-07-19
content:
Purpose:
Capture a compact, actionable synthesis of frontline feedback gathered during the July sprint window (2026-07-01 → 2026-07-17). This is a working brief for the cross-functional probe work (CS + Product + Eng) we want to kick off next week.

Context & framing:
- We pulled 42 discrete customer threads from Support, AM notes, and Sales calls where users raised operational friction or asked for specific feature levers. Rather than rehashing each thread, this doc stitches 6 vignettes that exemplify recurring tradeoffs: latency vs cost, model consistency across Dedicated/Private, embedding freshness, and observability gaps.
- Goal: propose 6 micro-probes (MVP experiments) with clear success metrics. Keep probes short (1–3 sprints) and low engineering risk where possible.

Topline synthesis (one-liners):
1) "Cold cache spikes users" — Customers see occasional 2–4x latency spikes after idle periods; they ask for simpler cache priming controls and visibility.
2) "Embedding drift pain" — Teams using embeddings for search notice quality drop after retraining models or rolling quantized variants. They want lineage and quick reindex hooks.
3) "Dedicated behavior mismatch" — Some infra teams report different response distributions between Hosted and Dedicated for the same pinned model/version.
4) "Billing surprise points" — Customers misinterpret token accounting when retries, tool-calls, or streaming chunks occur; requests for per-request sample breakdowns and CSV export.
5) "Rate-limit UX" — Sudden 429s from autoscale-burst transitions have poor telemetry and weak retry guidance.
6) "Eval leak-throughs" — Regression alerts trigger late because eval input coverage is out of sync with production prompt patterns.

Representative vignettes (annotated):
- Vignette A (SaaS search platform): large embedding index, weekly reindex. After a quantized model rollout (v2-q4) they reported a 12% drop in top-k recall. Root cause suspected: tokenization differences + vector normalization mismatch. Ask: lightweight reindex hook + a before/after sample-checker.
- Vignette B (customer support automation): intermittent 3s latency spikes between 2am–5am PST when traffic is low. Investigated: GPU warm-start policy + KV cache TTL. Ask: expose a "cache-warm" policy and a synthetic priming API that can be scheduled.
- Vignette C (regulated fintech): needs deterministic outputs across Hosted/Dedicated for auditability. Noticed small output variance on canonical prompts. Ask: deterministic seeding mode and an artifact proving sameness (hash of token logits or normalized output).

Candidate micro-probes (priority + quick description):
1) Cache-Warm API probe (priority: high) — provide a simple endpoint that primes model KV and prefix caches for a given prompt set; add a small telemetry flag so we can measure pre/post latency for primed sessions. Success metric: reduce median cold-start latency by >=30% for customers using the probe over 7 days. Owner: Eng-SRE + CS lead.

2) Embedding Reindex Diff Tool (priority: high) — a lightweight service that runs sample queries against old/new embedding variants and summarizes top-k overlap, cosine shift histograms, and a simple pass/fail threshold. Success metric: produce a human-readable diff report in <10s for a 100-sample set. Owner: Applied ML (Diego) + Product-Optimize.

3) Billing Transparency CSV export (priority: medium) — create per-request breakdowns (prompt tokens, completion tokens, tool-calls, retries) and an export button in Console. Success metric: reduce billing-related Support tickets by 40% in pilot cohort. Owner: Product + Billing.

4) Deterministic-compare mode for Dedicated (priority: medium) — sample-mode where runtime returns a deterministic hash (logits checksum or normalized string) alongside response; used for audits. Success metric: run 100 canonical prompts and show parity >= 99% between Hosted and Dedicated. Owner: Serving Runtime + Private Deployments.

5) Rate-limit guidance & graceful backoff (priority: medium) — detect autoscale-burst 429 patterns and return richer Retry-After hints + sample exponential backoff policy in SDK. Success metric: reduce repeated 429s per request by 60% and decrease confusing Support threads. Owner: Developer Experience + Console.

6) Eval shadow coverage probe (priority: low) — a small harness that captures production prompt fingerprints and flags prompts not covered by current eval suites. Success metric: identify top 10 uncovered prompt clusters in pilot accounts. Owner: Research/Applied ML + Product QA.

Low-effort MVT ideas (quick wins):
- Console toggle to "show token breakdown" for a single request in logs (UI only change).
- Slack notification rule for the CS-oncall whenever a dedicated deployment shows >5% change in distribution for canonical prompts.

Risk & open questions:
- Privacy: any production prompt capture for eval coverage must be opt-in and scrub PII. Need legal sign-off for telemetry scope.
- Engineering cost: some probes require runtime changes vs. Console/SDK changes. We should batch runtime probes to the next minor.
- Observability noise: adding new telemetry flags can increase noise; define storage TTL and sampling rates upfront.

Next steps (0–2 weeks):
- Friday 2026-07-23: cross-functional sync (CS, Eng-SRE, Applied ML, Product) to pick 3 probes for alpha. (Action: Maya to book)
- By 2026-07-30: prototype Cache-Warm API and Embedding Reindex Diff scripts as internal-only tools. (Owners: Eng-SRE, Diego)
- Legal review for prompt-capture and telemetry by 2026-08-06. (Owner: Aisha)

Appendix: sample customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We can't afford the jump in recall after a model roll — gives us buyer churn risk." — large marketplace
- "Our infra team saw little differences between hosted & dedicated; we need a simple way to assert sameness." — fintech
- "Billing CSVs would let us cross-check our usage internally — we get surprised by tool-call counts." — mid-market customer

Quick links & notes:
- Raw threads pulled from Slack + Zendesk: folder link in Confluence (linked above).
- Minimal prototype for embedding-diff available at the GitHub link (PR 48) — includes sample notebook and visualization.

Notes to self:
- Keep probes scoped small; prefer a quick UX toggle or script over long platform work unless ROI is clear.
- After pilots, bake successful probes into "Optimize" playbook with recommended defaults and SLOs.
summary: Working synthesis of July sprint feedback; 6 micro-probes proposed (cache-warm, embedding diff, billing CSV, deterministic compare, rate-limit guidance, eval coverage) with owners, success metrics, and next steps.
